**Checking the boxed formula**

With \(M=r/(s-1)\), a sequence is unique iff for every \(n\): \(\alpha_n>0\Rightarrow T_n>M-1\) and \(\alpha_n<r\Rightarrow T_n<1\), where \(T_n=\sum_{k\ge1}\alpha_{n+k}s^{-k}\). Two consequences follow:

- A digit 0 at position \(n\) forces all earlier digits to be 0, since \(M/s\le M-1\) when \(r\ge s\). Symmetrically, a digit \(r\) forces all earlier digits to be \(r\). Apart from prefixes of 0s or \(r\)s, which only give countably many bi-Lipschitz copies and do not change the dimension, the free part uses digits from a middle block.
- The surviving middle digits form a symmetric block \(\{k,\dots,r-k\}\), which has \(r-2k+1\) elements. The threshold \(k=\lfloor s(M-1)\rfloor=\lfloor s(r-s+1)/(s-1)\rfloor\) matches the proposed formula. I did not fully derive that the block is exactly \(\{k,\dots,r-k\}\), so this step rests partly on the proposed solution's structure and on my recollection of the literature on univoque sets.
